cl_xc_music.q: Does music change how a psychedelic session goes?
cl_xc_music.short: In one small study, patients said music changed their session, mostly in good ways.
cl_xc_music.but: None of the studies we read compared sessions with and without music.
how: 19 patients with hard-to-treat depression took psilocybin in a clinic with the same music. One patient got different music the second time.
Almost all said the music helped at times; about half said it sometimes made things harder.
Patients who spoke more warmly about the music had a bigger drop in depression a week later. But both were measured at the same time.
In a US survey, people who linked their hardest time to the music did not rate it as harder than others did.

cl_ket_music.q: Does music change how a ketamine session goes?
cl_ket_music.short: Nobody knows yet. In most studies, ketamine was given with other medicines during surgery or tests.
cl_ket_music.but: One review gathered these studies but did not check how good they were. A 2024 trial is not included yet.
how: A review found 14 studies of music with ketamine, all with patients in clinics or trials.
In most, ketamine was given with other medicines during surgery or tests. There, music often went with less worry or pain than no music.
Only one study of ketamine alone had a group that heard nothing. Children who heard their mother's voice were less anxious than that group.
Up to the end of 2023, the review found no study comparing music with no music in ketamine treatment for depression. A 2024 trial has not been read here yet.

cl_mdma_response_predictors.q: Why do some people feel MDMA more strongly than others?
cl_mdma_response_predictors.short: In lab studies, how strong MDMA felt went most with the amount per kilo of body weight.
cl_mdma_response_predictors.but: Healthy young volunteers in a hospital, most trying MDMA for the first time.
how: 194 healthy young adults took MDMA in hospital, one set amount each time. On another day they took a dummy pill.

The amount for each kilo of body weight went most with how strong it felt. Women and men did not clearly differ once weight was counted. An earlier report from the same lab suggested women may feel more bad effects.
People who tend to worry, or who felt anxious and low just before, said they felt more anxious than calm people did. Open people felt closer to others.
Each session had one fixed amount, so what happens when someone who feels little takes more was not tested.

cl_lsd_response_predictors.q: Why do some people feel LSD more strongly than others?
cl_lsd_response_predictors.short: In lab studies, the dose went most with how strong LSD felt. Mood and personality did too.
cl_lsd_response_predictors.but: The paper says which way each link goes, not how big it is.
how: 213 healthy adults took LSD in a hospital room and, in most studies, a dummy pill on another day.
People who felt well just before had stronger effects than others. People who felt anxious had more anxiety during the session.
Open people had more spiritual feelings. People who had used drugs like LSD more often felt less overall than people who had used them less.
People whose genes make a liver enzyme slower had more LSD in the blood. Each session had one fixed dose, so taking more was not tested.
